title: Low-Margin Branch Points in Deterministic LLM Deliberation
summary: Deterministic multi-agent LLM deliberation can exactly re- play a fixed transcript, yet exact replay alone does not test local resistance to controlled internal interventions. Because each response becomes context for later agents, a changed greedy token can redirect a transcript-mediated execution. We present a white-box audit of this local failure mode in a five-agent committee under greedy decoding. We prospectively select low- and high-margin token positions, require exact no-op re- play, inject norm-relative residual displacements, and measure first transcript divergence within ten generated tokens. Low- margin positions are more branch-sensitive than high-margin controls, while matched margin-reducing gradient directions branch substantially more often than margin-increasing con- trols. We then continue selected realized branches through the committee to distinguish textual persistence from preference and final-decision changes. The contribution is a controlled audit for local branch susceptibility in this specified protocol, not an estimate of deployment frequency, decision correct- ness, or a phenomenon unique to multi-agent systems.

title: Deterministic $n^{O(\log n)}$ Graph Isomorphism Algorithm via Inherited Decompositions
summary: We give a deterministic $n^{O(\log d)}$-time algorithm for isomorphism of graphs with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $d$. Since $d<n$, this is an $n^{O(\log n)}$-time algorithm for graph isomorphism. To our knowledge, this is the first proof of such a worst-case bound for general graphs. It improves the explicit cubic logarithmic exponent in the analysis of the corrected Luks--Babai algorithm. For graphs of maximum degree $d$, the best previous bound known to us, due to Grohe, Neuen, and Schweitzer, is $n^{O((\log d)^c)}$ for an absolute constant $c$. The algorithm uses the local-certificate and color-refinement steps of Babai's quasipolynomial algorithm, but retains the decomposition of each recursive instance when it solves an auxiliary coloring problem. There are two reasons for retaining this information. First, a local test can make progress without removing many vertices: it can eliminate a layer of permutation symmetry. A logarithmic bound on the total weight of these layers allows tests of constant size. Second, the auxiliary bipartite graphs arising in the symmetry-breaking step can be represented inside the current instance, after retaining a row decomposition when necessary. These recursive calls inherit the progress already made. Two further observations give the dependence on the degree. The recursive calls made by a local test check disjoint parts of the instance, so together they cost about as much as one call on the whole instance. And for graphs of maximum degree $d$, each large symmetric action that the algorithm must break acts on at most $d$ points. We present the algorithm through colorings, partitions, and bipartite graphs, and collect the permutation-group ingredients in one appendix. The result extends to string isomorphism and returns one isomorphism and generators for the full automorphism group.

title: Stand-In Effects and Pooling Amplification: Lessons from Biological World Models for Testing Action Effects
comments: v3: adds a second registered test on two further published world-model families (IRIS, TD-MPC2; OSF j75g2), exploratory studies of score rule, sampling noise, regimes and validation tuning on ERK data, and corrections. 100 pages
summary: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly trained on data from randomized experiments, and whether their predictions respond to actions is usually checked by replacing or removing the actions and measuring the loss in accuracy. Taking biological experiments as the guiding case, we show that such diagnostics report action effects where there are none: under autocorrelated designs, future actions stand in for history the model does not see. When the design law is known, a conditional randomization test written as an e-value is valid in finite samples whatever the model, provided the resampler conditions on the full state the design used. A second failure arises whenever many sites share one action sequence, as in world models: the pooled score turns small model errors along the action contrast into overwhelming evidence against a true effect. In a pixel world, its median log e-value fell from -17.3 to -6832 as frames grew from 64 to 4096 pixels, while the oracle's rose. Tempering the score changes the bet, not the validity. Our own preregistered analysis of optogenetic ERK experiments failed in exactly this way; a tempered statistic, registered before the data were obtained, then rejected the null on a never-opened field (E = 1.1e10). Every single tempering factor we tried, estimated from residuals or tuned on validation data, collapsed in some setting; mixtures over a fixed grid of factors never did. In registered tests on three world-model families trained by others, the pooled test rejected in 0 of 96 units of a diffusion model in which actions mattered, and reached the registered power bar in 10 of 26 Atari games under IRIS's own token likelihood and 1 of 6 control tasks under TD-MPC2; mixtures fixed in advance reached it in all 96 units, 24 of 26 games and 6 of 6 tasks. Under exact nulls the statistics made 4 rejections in 22,848 tests.
comment: v3: adds a second registered test on two further published world-model families (IRIS, TD-MPC2; OSF j75g2), exploratory studies of score rule, sampling noise, regimes and validation tuning on ERK data, and corrections. 100 pages

title: A Global Routing Method for Electronic Circuit Design Integrating Flow Matching and Constrained A*
summary: Global routing is a fundamental issue in the design of electronic circuits, as it directly relates to the efficiency, reliability, and compactness of the overall layout of integrated systems. As the demand for higher functionality and reliability within a limited chip area increases, the importance of routing as a design consideration has never been greater. Efficient global routing optimization techniques are therefore required to connect all pins with minimal wirelength (WL), while avoiding congestion and interference across multiple nets within the design space. As the number of nets to be routed increases, global routing inherently suffers from a combinatorial explosion in the design space, making it increasingly difficult to obtain feasible solutions. In this paper, we focus on solving constrained global routing problems based on a heuristic A*-based framework. Based on this concept, a hybrid approach is proposed by integrating constrained A* with flow matching (FM). The method utilizes FM to construct a global cost map that captures routing tendencies across the design space, which is then used to guide the constrained A* search process. This enables efficient exploration of the solution space while satisfying routing constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable WL and via usage to baseline methods while maintaining constraint satisfaction across a wide range of scenarios. Notably, the framework shows strong capability in solving complex routing instances that are difficult to handle using conventional approaches. Additionally, the method shows robust generalization performance across different problem sizes and net configurations.

title: MAGAR: Multimodal Agents for GUI-Based 3D Mechanical Assembly and Minimal Rework
summary: A GUI command can be correct at the interface level yet still produce an incorrect assembly. An agent must identify the relevant components, respect their structural relationships, and determine which parts should move during recovery. We introduce MAGAR-Bench, a benchmark of 4,000 multimodal samples from 26 assembly families that separates Assembly Decision, Atomic Action, and Minimal Rework. For rework, the objective counts distinct moved parts within the validated recovery candidate set for each state, rather than the number of actions. We also introduce MAGAR, a selective correction framework built on a frozen policy obtained by supervised fine-tuning. Its key design matches correction granularity to output dependencies. Structured candidates revise assembly fields and rework scope, while complete action candidates keep native GUI primitives coupled with their parameters. A learned selector retains the original prediction unless a candidate passes a task-specific intervention threshold. On recorded states from held-out assembly families, MAGAR improves Overall, the task-balanced aggregate, from 37.50 to 41.39, with gains on all three tasks. Across 209 interventions, 70 correct an error and 22 introduce one. These results support task-specific correction while highlighting the remaining tradeoff between fixing errors and preserving reliable predictions.

title: FORGE: Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly
summary: Large language models have demonstrated strong capabilities in structured reasoning and code generation, yet identifying an assembly fault does not guarantee the ability to generate executable rework programs. In interlocking assemblies, a locally plausible repair program may violate blocking dependencies, omit required recovery operations, or terminate in an incorrect configuration. We identify this challenge as fault-conditioned executable rework generation, where models must jointly reason about structural failures and generate programs that restore constrained assembly states. To benchmark this capability, we introduce FORGE-Bench, containing 4,000 tasks across 26 interlocking assemblies with five assemblies held out for evaluating generalization to unseen structures. We further propose FORGE (Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly), a structured state-to-program framework that decomposes rework generation into Rework Structuring and Action Grounding. Rework Structuring captures fault-induced recovery dependencies, while Action Grounding maps these dependencies into state-conditioned executable actions. Experiments show that locally reasonable repair code is insufficient for reliable assembly recovery, and that connecting structural recovery reasoning with executable action realization is essential for verified target restoration.

title: FindLink: Learning to Assess Scientific Connections from Source-Grounded Premises
summary: Scientific discovery from the literature requires assessing connections among findings obtained under different study conditions. Source attribution makes individual findings traceable, but does not determine what they jointly support. We introduce GI-TraceBench, a benchmark of 10,282 questions in gastrointestinal oncology that unifies provenance question answering, knowledge discovery, and hypothesis evaluation through shared Paper, Claim, and Evidence Span records. We further propose FindLink, a two-stage framework for provenance-grounded scientific reasoning. Premise Grounding constructs source-bound premises with explicit study context and support status. Structured Reasoning organizes these premises into support plans that represent both supported relations and unresolved conditions, then generates evidence-conditioned answers using deterministic compiler feedback. The compiler verifies structural and source-binding consistency, but does not assess scientific entailment. On the 1,545-question fixed-evidence test set, FindLink improves the balanced family macro score from 67.95 to 87.25 over direct supervised fine-tuning of the same backbone. A retrained variant without Structured Reasoning achieves slightly higher premise-identifier F1, but substantially lower relation and evidence-sufficiency F1. These results indicate that scientific reasoning requires not only identifying grounded premises, but also assessing what connections those premises support.

title: AGiR: Mitigating Gift Over-Reliance in Mixed-Motive Games
summary: In this paper, we consider mixed-motive games (MMGs) which model various real-world multi-agent scenarios where self-interested agents must both cooperate and compete. We identify an issue with existing gifting methods, where agents become overly dependent on incoming gifts and fail to learn reward-yielding behaviors, a phenomenon we call gift over-reliance. To address this, we propose a refusal-augmented gifting framework that balances cooperation and competition in MMGs. Our approach introduces an adaptive refusal mechanism that allows agents to selectively reject a portion of received gifts from their policy-update signals, thereby mitigating gift over-reliance and preventing the agents from being exploited by other agents. This mechanism is gifting-method-agnostic, serving as a plug-in for existing schemes while enabling decentralized learning. We demonstrate that across diverse MMG environments and gifting schemes, our mechanism consistently reduces gift over-reliance and prevents lock-in to sacrificing policies, improving $α$-fairness as a result, without necessitating major changes to existing training pipelines.

title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
comments: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions. A tuned robust predictor was also safe with synchronous switching, but not with per-rotor jitter.
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

title: Mass Scaling Laws for Energy-Optimal Horizontal Multirotor Flight
comments: Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, October 2026
summary: Multicopters are a type of aerial robot seeing extensive real-world applications but with range and endurance as critical bottlenecks. Optimization of its energy efficiency through energy-aware flight planning (e.g. cruise speed-scheduling) has hence been an important topic. The mass of the multicopter is an important factor to consider, as it has a significant impact on efficiency, and many common applications are subject to frequent mass variation due to payload change. This work derives closed-form scaling relationships between the energy-optimal steady horizontal flight behavior of a multicopter and its vehicle mass, and validates them experimentally on two multirotor platforms. Specifically, for mass-only variation, i.e., when payload changes the vehicle mass while the airframe geometry, aerodynamic characteristics, and rotor configuration remain unchanged, we show through a combination of numerical simulation, theoretical derivation, and experimental validation that (1) the energy-optimal velocity is proportional to the square root of vehicle mass; (2) the energy-optimal pitch angle is constant with respect to mass; and (3) the optimal energy per meter is proportional to mass. The analysis shows that these three relationships arise from a common mass-similarity property of the steady-state flight and rotor-aerodynamic equations. Furthermore, the obtained scaling relationships enable simple yet effective cruise-speed planning to optimize energy efficiency and extend the range and endurance of the multicopter.
comment: Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, October 2026

title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks
summary: Large language models are candidates for collecting and analyzing records in criminal investigations and mass surveillance. Their capability and accuracy in this work cannot currently be measured. Real deployments lack the ground truth needed to score a model's conclusions, and no benchmark evaluates these capabilities in a simulated environment. We present Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine, and KierstonBench, a benchmark that tests these capabilities against known simulated events. Kierston models approximately 125,000 residents of Allentown, Pennsylvania, generating their daily activities and the telecommunications, financial, administrative and license-plate records that surveillance and investigative systems collect about them. These records derive from a common behavioral timeline and are distributed across sources representing separate providers. Models investigate through a restricted records interface, linking observations across sources without access to the underlying simulation. The benchmark comprises 32 task families covering record linkage, routine reconstruction, incident investigation and assessment of deceptive accounts. In an evaluation of sixteen language models, most could not perform records investigation and submitted identifications the records did not support. A small number of frontier models solved most of the tasks and abstained when evidence was insufficient. In some cases these models still fell for common deceptions and assumptions, and none replaced an investigator.

title: Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data
summary: Accurate vegetation-encroachment assessment and risk mitigation require electric utilities to accurately locate and characterize distribution-network assets, including poles and power lines, and distinguish among medium-voltage, low-voltage, neutral, and telecommunication lines. Mobile and aerial Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds provide detailed 3D representations of these assets and their surroundings. However, power-line detection and reconstruction remain challenging because conductor returns are often sparse, incomplete, noisy, or occluded by vegetation. These challenges are especially significant in distribution networks, where lower pole heights and complex line configurations place conductors close to trees. In addition, mobile and aerial LiDAR datasets differ substantially in point density, viewing geometry, spatial coverage, and occlusion patterns. We propose a robust and automated reconstruction method combining scaled density-based clustering, robust polynomial fitting, and iterative fragment merging to recover individual conductors under severe data incompleteness and occlusion. Following semantic classification, the same reconstruction pipeline processes both mobile and aerial LiDAR data without modality-specific code or parameter tuning. The method is evaluated through degradation experiments, benchmarking, parameter sensitivity analysis, and large-scale validation. On the aerial dataset, it achieves 96.87% precision, 96.66% recall, a 96.76% F$_1$-score, and a geometric RMSE of 0.127 m. On the mobile dataset, where conductor-level reference annotations were unavailable, it achieves a point-to-model RMSE of 0.045 m and a reconstruction coverage of 95.27%. Source code, documentation, and evaluation data are publicly available at https://github.com/varen-project.

title: Whose Guardrail? User Identity Shapes the Effectiveness of Model Disclaimers in Mitigating LLM Political Persuasion
comments: Correction were made to the appendix, citations, and author list
summary: Politically biased AI can shift users' opinions, yet it remains unclear whether model disclaimers protect against such persuasion. We report a preregistered experiment (N=1,586) examining how disclaimer design and user characteristics shape susceptibility to politically biased AI. We varied whether disclaimers identified political bias versus potential inaccuracies and whether they included an explanation. Participants completed two decision-making tasks with an LLM biased against their political views, with outcomes assessed immediately and one week later. Disclaimers identifying political bias and including an explanation reduced persuasion, but effects varied across contexts and did not persist. Individual differences were more consistent predictors: Republicans were more persuaded and reported higher trust than Democrats across tasks. Similarly, participants who used AI more frequently were also more persuaded, whereas those with greater self-reported AI knowledge were less persuaded. These findings suggest that generic disclaimers are not enough: effective safeguards must account for user heterogeneity and context.
comment: Correction were made to the appendix, citations, and author list

title: Recasting Visual Language Models as EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Neurodiagnostics
summary: Historically automated electroencephalography (EEG) systems was done using task-specific supervised models trained on purposely annotated data. A more recent modeling paradigm relies on creating a unified representation, or a 'foundation model', for multiple modality-specific tasks through large-scale domain-specific pretraining on the unannotated EEG signal. The quality of this unified representation directly depends on the availability of the modality-specific datasets. At the same time, generalist Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit broad few-shot learning capacities as well as good fine-tuning adaptability to different visual and language tasks. Can VLMs learn how to read and interpret EEG visually, emulating to a degree the way human clinicians inspect the EEG patterns? In this work we make a case that they can: we show that generalist VLMs without large-scale EEG pretraining perform competitively across a collection of clinical neuro-diagnostic tasks, can adapt to different tasks in a few-shot learning setting better than specialist foundation models, and exhibit better performance with model scaling when modality-specific models fail to exhibit.

title: Combining Relevant Expert Knowledge Using Mixtures of Feedback Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
summary: A neuro-symbolic system should combine only relevant answers from expert agents or other knowledge sources. Using only relevant experts for a given input query becomes ever more important for accuracy and scalability as the knowledge network grows and connects ever more knowledge sources. We extend the standard definition of relevance from the legal theory of evidence: An answer is relevant if and only if it is both probative and material for the matter at hand given the knowledge available. We apply this relevancy scheme to mixing the feedback fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) of real or artificial experts. The expert FCM directed causal graphs mix or combine into a common knowledge network. We compare the equilibrium limit-cycle predictions or answers of the experts to the answers of the mixture FCM and then estimate the probative status of answers by their difference or variation. A new Bayes-like theorem de-mixes the knowledge mixture into corresponding posterior-like FCMs that also allow relevancy-based comparisons. The result is a final set of relevancy mixing weights that produces a relevancy-mixed FCM knowledge network for the given query. So different queries produce different relevancy-mixed FCMs. We demonstrate this relevancy approach using generated synthetic FCMs from an actual 13-node expert FCM that models the causes and feedbacks of ischemic-stroke risk.

title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
comments: 68 pages, 5 figures, 31 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/junbolian/JointDW
summary: Dantzig--Wolfe reformulation strengthens the linear relaxation of a mixed-integer program by convexifying constraint families, and each candidate costs a column generation run. The choice is hard when families strengthen the bound only together, as in classical lot-sizing, network-design, and facility-location formulations. We prove that when an evaluation convexifies at most $s$ of $k$ families, methods that observe only bounds need of order $k^w$ evaluations to find a hidden group of $w$ families in the worst case. A prediction missing $e$ members reduces this to $Θ(k^e)$ through a staged search that need not know $e$. The orders extend to several groups, prices, and growing evaluation costs. We study two predictors: a lookahead at an optimal LP dual, which vanishes on groups whose families share no variable, and language models reading the model, verified by the staged search in JointDW. Such groups appear in three of ten MIPLIB-NL models whose bound can be improved and in all 59 benchmark instances. Given the coefficients of models with up to 16 families, one language model names a true group first in 249 of 252 answers. On the benchmark instances, decompositions chosen by language models from the text solve faster than those of GCG's detector.
comment: 68 pages, 5 figures, 31 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/junbolian/JointDW

title: EEGDash Corpus: A Training-Ready Public Corpus for EEG Foundation Models
comments: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the Workshop on Machine Learning for EEG Signal Processing (MLESP 2026), IEEE BIBM 2026
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on tens of thousands of hours. The largest clinical archives restrict redistribution, while public datasets use different formats and licences. Here, we rebuild the 77 redistributable datasets of the REVE pretraining corpus that reach its 200 Hz input (14,075 hours across 7,272 subjects) and release them as eegdash-corpus-v0, with raw-file access by name through EEGDash and a checksummed Zarr store on Hugging Face, converted with REVE's preprocessing recipe. Every dataset keeps its licence, and any subset of datasets can be selected by name. To test whether this public store pretrains REVE-Base, we train the model twice from scratch with REVE's trainer and score it on seven public OpenEEGBench tasks. First, under linear probing, the frozen encoder reaches 0.331 in chance-adjusted balanced accuracy, against 0.333 for the released model (untrained: 0.200), a difference smaller than the spread between our two pretraining seeds. Second, after fine-tuning, it reaches 0.273 against 0.325 published (0.301 in our rerun), and part of this gap comes from the scoring pipeline. A public, training-ready EEG corpus can therefore pretrain the frozen representations of a foundation model and provide a shared base that other groups can audit.
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the Workshop on Machine Learning for EEG Signal Processing (MLESP 2026), IEEE BIBM 2026

title: $A^3$-VLA: Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation
summary: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) enable robots to perform manipulation tasks by leveraging Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to process visual observations and language instructions. However, the action prediction objective itself lacks fine-grained task-specific perceptual supervision, making it prone to relying on task-irrelevant visual shortcuts, leading attention away from target objects and key interaction areas, thereby limiting its operational performance and generalization ability. To address this, we propose Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation ($A^3$-VLA), a framework that derives task-specific visual guidance from the manipulation process itself. Specifically, $A^3$-VLA first generates heuristic candidate regions for target objects and the robot from interaction-induced visual changes, and refines them with a visual segmentation model offline. These regions serve as explicit perceptual guidance through two complementary objectives: an attention allocation loss that encourages sufficient focus on task-critical regions when language or robot state tokens query the visual input, and a contrastive learning loss that aligns the representations of candidate target regions with language instructions while separating them from task-irrelevant regions. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that $A^3$-VLA consistently improves multiple VLA backbones, with an average success rate gain of 6.5% - 25.2% across benchmarks.

title: Dynamic Shape Control of Soft Trunk Robots
summary: Controlling the shape profile of soft trunk robots extends their reach into complex regions of the workspace and enhances their use in practical applications. Recent advances in soft robot design have enabled soft trunk robots to achieve greater flexibility in conforming to complex shapes. Specifically, trunk robots whose geometries are designed as helicoids have been shown to enable extreme shape-changing capabilities. Their compliance makes them highly nonlinear, which in turn makes shape control difficult. On similar tendon-driven trunk robots, model-based controllers based on the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) have achieved high accuracy in closed-loop end-effector tracking. We extend this approach by learning an aSSM model of the full body of a trimmed-helicoid soft trunk robot from data and use this in a model predictive control (MPC) scheme to demonstrate a range of shape control tasks on hardware. On closed-loop dynamic shape regulation, our method outperforms the available linear baselines by a factor of 10. In human-in-the-loop interactive demos, our method completes section-by-section shaping and balances a tennis ball for over 25 seconds, while the linear baselines fall short. A model-free reinforcement learning policy trained for 12 hours on hardware fails on the same balancing task. These results establish aSSM-based MPC as a practical route to full-body shape control on real soft hardware.

title: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
comments: 8 pages main body, 10 pages appendix, 1 figure
summary: Tech-facilitated gender based violence (TFGBV) is a pervasive online harm affecting women and gender minority groups through its many direct and covert forms. Current models and annotated datasets for gendered harm detection are dominated by data from, and models trained in, Global North languages. In collaboration with civil society organizations (CSOs) from Jordan, Francophone West Africa, and Kenya, we developed a community-led approach to crowdsource culturally and linguistically relevant instances of TFGBV in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili. We annotated the crowdsourced data using active learning to develop a small but performant dataset (N=3022) called ALTO to improve TFGBV detection in the three languages. Through benchmarking and fine-tuning experiments, we show that existing harmful content detection models show poor TFGBV recall within ALTO and improve with fine-tuning. We found that models often miss covert harms across all languages, while error rates are markedly higher in Swahili. We report the experimental results and release the annotation taxonomy, dataset, and trained models.
comment: 8 pages main body, 10 pages appendix, 1 figure

title: Integrated Identity Protection for Semantic Communications in Embodied IoT Systems
summary: Embodied Internet of Things (IoT) systems are promoting the adoption of task-oriented semantic communication (SemCom), in which the trustworthy task decisions increasingly require both semantic reliability and source legitimacy. However, existing trustworthy SemCom designs mainly focus on semantic content recovery and protection, with limited attention to source identity protection. Motivated by this limitation, this paper establishes a new information exploitation perspective for integrated SemCom-identity protection that leverages task-level error tolerance to coordinate semantic information and source identity information carried by the same waveform. We first examine these two information resources and then analyze their integration feasibility at the observation, processing, and decision levels. To exploit these resources for different identity protection objectives, we further develop a dual-branch identity protection mechanism with two operating modes. In the authentication mode, semantic recovery and physical-layer source verification are performed in parallel using the same received observation. In the concealment mode, identity exposure is suppressed while semantic reconstruction quality is maintained to support anonymous transmission. Finally, two representative case studies on active source impersonation and passive identity inference are presented to evaluate the proposed framework.

title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
summary: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.

title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
summary: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then constructs compressed weights and executable inference code. The agent controls its algorithm and experiments; perplexity feedback guides search, and independent verification checks the final model. Across six agents and six model--size settings, 29 of 36 submissions pass verification. Selecting the lowest-perplexity agent design per task yields an average 3.4% perplexity increase over BF16 and 77.33% downstream accuracy, compared with 79.56% for BF16. Recorded experiments reveal how agents achieve these outcomes and where improvement breaks down. Agents lower PPL in 21 of 24 revisions at nearly fixed storage; complete-model feedback reverses 17 of 79 prior local rankings; and generation and inference tests expose failures that likelihood alone misses. The results identify representation design, experimental judgment, and capability validation as central to agent-driven model compression, a measurable component of efficiency-oriented self-improvement.

title: cuRoboV2-Fast: Fast Torque-Limited Collision-Free Motion Planning
summary: We present cuRoboV2-Fast, a GPU-accelerated planner that reduces both planning latency and execution time for collision-free, payload-aware, torque-limited motions. B-spline trajectory optimization reduces the required iterations, while accelerated robot computations and differentiable inverse dynamics reduce refinement cost and accommodate changing payloads. TimeOpt optimizes traversal speed along the fixed path under sampled velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque constraints, exploiting local spline support to solve banded Newton systems efficiently on the GPU. With a 3,kg payload, cuRoboV2-Fast achieves 4.4 ms mean planning time on RTX 5090, 14.7x faster than cuRoboV2. Our method on Jetson AGX Orin plans faster than cuRoboV1 + TOPPRA on RTX 5090. A stereo-camera-based deployment on YAM achieves 5.93 s mean completed pick-and-drop cycles, 34.6% shorter than cuRoboV2. Code (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/NVlabs/curobo , Project Page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/lpr/curobov2-fast .

title: Selective Retrieval Routing for Multi-Violation Knowledge Graph Repair
summary: Knowledge graphs often contain missing or inconsistent facts that undermine the applications built on them. Schema validation detects such violations but does not identify which of several valid repairs recovers the intended graph. External corpora can supply the evidence needed to identify the intended repair, but retrieving from them is costly and not always successful. We propose a framework for selective retrieval in iterative graph repair. An LLM repair agent explores and edits the graph, while a router controls its access to a researcher agent that retrieves external evidence. We extend a violation-injection framework to generate cases with multiple compatible violations and known reference repairs. The agent's repair outcomes on these cases provide supervision for training the deployment-specific router. On two building-automation datasets, researcher access improves repairs for some violations and degrades them for others, with effects differing across deployments. The router uses fewer repair-time tokens than always enabling access in all six evaluation suites. It achieves higher repair $F_1$ than always disabling access in five of six suites.

title: Volatility Heredity in Multivariate Time Series: A Statistically Guided Temporal Convolutional Approach to Variable Ordering
summary:
Volatility heredity concerns the information that past fluctuations in one series may carry about another after accounting for the target's own persistence. QS-TCN compares this dependence in both directions to estimate an order of temporal precedence. For each series, quasi-maximum likelihood estimation yields a persistence coefficient, and the matrix pencil method extracts temporal modes from the autocovariances of squared observations. These estimates define filters in a temporal convolutional network. The network models the target's squared observations from their own past and scores the association between the residuals and the filtered history of a candidate source. Differences between the two directional scores are aggregated into a global order.
  In an exploratory simulation with 100 systems in each of four volatility regimes, an ensemble of ten models trained with fixed seeds achieved higher mean ordering quality than CCF-AUC, a lead--lag method based on distance correlation, in every regime. Against CCF-AUC applied to squared standardized observations, the mean gains were 8.69 percentage points under positive linear coupling and 7.81 points when nonlinear coupling depended on the target's state. In the other two regimes, paired 95\% bootstrap intervals for the gains included zero. Mean agreement with reference constraints was 71.55\% across nine Finance systems and 54.02\% across 27 simulated functional magnetic resonance imaging systems, compared with 50\% expected under random ordering. In a panel of daily currency and gold returns, the estimated order placed the dollar--franc and dollar--yen exchange rates before gold.

title: Adjustment-Anchor Dependence in Formulaic Alpha Languages: A Certified Grammar and a Re-Anchoring Audit
comments: 41 pages (12 main text, 29 supplementary), 7 main-text figures, 7 main-text tables. Revised the manuscript and figures and included supplementary material
summary: Several public scripts for formulaic alpha mining store prices adjusted to the snapshot's last day, so a past day's stored price changes with every later split or dividend and formulas that do not cancel the adjustment factor depend on future corporate actions. We formalise a change of adjustment anchor as a per-stock group action and give a two-sorted type system that soundly certifies anchor invariance from a formula's syntax, under a declared field-adjustment contract and idealised operator semantics; its second sort admits log-returns, and a linear-time checker plugs into any miner. In a re-anchoring audit on Chinese A-shares, pools that five published methods mined in our benchmark pipeline score a mean information coefficient (IC) 0.005 higher on the stored representation than on a cutoff-anchored one, about 14% of their IC. The mean signed change for certified pools is about -0.001, and pools mined on past-anchored data stay sensitive. On the Chinese development folds, certification shows no detectable predictive cost or gain; the estimated minimum detectable difference is about 0.017 IC across cells on pool ICs of 0.03-0.04. We also trace an erroneous index-membership entry to public Qlib data snapshots and show that re-mining exposes the effect of such data defects, which re-evaluating fixed pools understates.
comment: 41 pages (12 main text, 29 supplementary), 7 main-text figures, 7 main-text tables. Revised the manuscript and figures and included supplementary material

title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
comments: 51 pages, 13 figures, 25 tables. Models and code: https://huggingface.co/nace-ai
summary: Autoregressive approaches with large language models, such as long chain-of-thought reasoning, have become the default for new AI applications because they reach higher accuracy on a wide range of tasks. In production, however, they give inconsistent answers, require parsing of outputs, and add cost and latency. Decision models address this: given a question and a set of options supplied by the user, they return a probability distribution over the options without autoregressive decoding. We present Drex, a family of four open decision models with 8B (DLM), 9B (v1.5), 35B with 3B active (v2.0), and 27B (Max) parameters. Each request consists of a state (a document, record, or agent context, optionally with images) and questions about it, each asking for a choice among options, a yes/no judgment, or a score on an ordered scale. Training combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF), plus vision tuning for Max. Ablations show that RLAF improves accuracy and that consistency losses improve robustness to option order. On Decision Index 0.4.1, Max sets a new state of the art among the decision models we compare (67.52 on the public suite vs. 60.70 for Jev 1.14.0). On Decision Bench v4, it is statistically tied with d3-turbo and GPT-6 Sol and trails Claude Opus 5.5 by 1.6 points, and it has the highest accuracy among decision models on DecideBench. Max answers a typical request in 183 ms, against about 2.0 s for GPT-6 Sol and 3.5 s for Claude Opus 5.5, and its outputs are stable under option reordering. All four models are open source: https://github.com/nace-ai/drex-decision-models
comment: 51 pages, 13 figures, 25 tables. Models and code: https://huggingface.co/nace-ai

title: Towards Scalable Diagnostic-Driven Whole-Slide Image Retrieval for Pathology Archives
summary: The growing adoption of digital pathology has rapidly expanded collections of hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images, yet efficient navigation through these archives remains challenging, as metadata is often inconsistent or unavailable. Content-based image retrieval addresses this challenge by identifying similar cases directly from visual representations instead of manual annotations or metadata. Existing retrieval systems have demonstrated promising performance but largely rely on handcrafted indexing pipelines and predefined sampling strategies, constraining scalability and generalization. Here, we present CLEAR-WSI (Constant-Length Embedding for Automatic Retrieval of Whole-Slide Images) as a scalable, diagnostic-driven slide-retrieval framework, validated on both public and clinical data. Using a fixed-length slide embedding, CLEAR-WSI refines retrieved candidates with either a predicted diagnostic label or the ground-truth label, depending on the retrieval setting. Newly processed cases are subsequently added to the expanding memory bank, allowing the retrieval archive to grow over time. On a comprehensive benchmark consisting of two public and one private clinical datasets representing four retrieval tasks, CLEAR-WSI improves Precision@5 over the strongest evaluated baseline, with gains on CAMELYON16 (3.10), BRACS-1 (2.75), BRACS-2 (1.95), and X-HER2 (3.75). Additional ablation and latency studies further examine the contribution of each component and highlight its potential for scalable deployment.

title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
summary: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, evaluating the correctness of their responses is crucial for reliable use. However, such evaluation is challenging because reference answers are rarely available in practice. Existing reference-free methods mainly rely on output signals, which may assign high scores to incorrect responses and thus do not necessarily reflect correctness. This motivates exploring the model's internal computation for complementary correctness signals. Recent studies exploit internal states, but they mainly analyze hidden-state trajectories across layers, which record only the combined updates of attention and feed-forward networks (FFNs) and overlook how these components interact. We therefore propose Circe, a training-free self-evaluation method that assesses a response using both internal and external signals, without reference answers or repeated sampling. For internal signals, we first introduce component interaction consistency (CIC), which measures the directional alignment between attention updates in earlier layers and attention-induced FFN output changes in later layers. We further incorporate representation geometry (RG) to characterize normalized displacement and angular changes along layerwise hidden-state trajectories. For the external signal, we convert the mean negative log-likelihood of generated tokens into a bounded likelihood confidence (LC) score. Finally, we fuse CIC, RG, and LC into a unified correctness score. Experiments on five LLMs and six benchmarks across four domains show that our method distinguishes correct from incorrect responses more effectively than existing baselines, and generalizes to multilingual, multimodal, and open-world settings.

title: An Integrated Open-Source Stack for Vision-Based Autonomous Navigation of Wheeled Rovers
summary: Vision-based rover autonomy requires integrating perception, localization, planning and platform-specific control under limited sensing and computing resources. We present an open-source ROS 2 stack for following directional arrows, reaching a terminal cone and returning autonomously to the start. It connects YOLOv8n detection and geometric direction, range and bearing estimation with RGB-D SLAM, wheel-inertial state estimation, kinematics-aware planning, behavior-tree mission management and STM32 actuation. Standard interfaces separate reusable autonomy from the hardware layer; a proportional path-following plugin supports low-speed rover motion. Public resources include software, configuration, a labeled dataset, trained weights and evaluation logs. On 478 held-out images, the detector achieves mAP@0.5 of 0.720 under the Ultralytics evaluator and outperforms a classical OpenCV baseline under a shared evaluation protocol. The reported perception latency is 25 ms on a Jetson Orin NX. Three missions, one indoor and two outdoor, demonstrate marker-guided navigation and autonomous return without operator motion commands or reported collisions. Field results document integration failures and corrective choices; repeated instrumented trials remain necessary to quantify physical navigation errors and reliability.

title: Meituan-Robotics-0: A Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Desktop Manipulation
summary: We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. MR0 combines 147 million vision-language samples with 15,060 hours of curated robot trajectories spanning 12 embodiments. A three-stage training recipe aligns multimodal representations with robot behavior through discrete action-token pre-training, transfers these priors to continuous cross-embodiment control through flow-matching mid-training, and adapts the policy through real-world post-training. We introduce Rollback, which pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to provide positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning or advantage labeling. A unified end-effector interface supports heterogeneous embodiments, while asynchronous action-chunk merging maintains smooth execution under variable inference latency. An event-driven agent maintains persistent task events and reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes, enabling cross-task retrieval and conditional task resumption. MR0 achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ranks fifth in the RoboDojo VLA track. Under matched HG-DAgger post-training, MR0 achieves higher average success rate and progress score than $π_{0.5}$ across three real-robot tasks. On Ethernet insertion, CFG-DAgger trained with Rollback data reaches 70% success and a progress score of 0.90. Qualitative agent deployments demonstrate cross-task event retrieval and recovery from temporarily unsatisfied task conditions.

AI.title_translation: 美团机器人-0：一种用于桌面操作的视觉-语言-动作基座模型
AI.tldr: 美团发布桌面操作VLA基座模型MR0，结合三阶段流匹配训练、Rollback人机交互修正与事件驱动架构，在仿真与真机任务上性能优异。
AI.motivation: 构建针对固定基座桌面操作的高泛化性视觉-语言-动作（VLA）基座模型，解决跨本体适配、推理延迟抖动，以及在真实人机纠错过程中高效利用正负反馈样本的难题。
AI.method:
1. 数据：整合1.47亿图文样本与跨12种本体的15,060小时机器人轨迹；
2. 训练机制：采用三阶段方案，即离散动作标记预训练、流匹配（flow-matching）中程连续控制迁移，以及真机后训练；
3. Rollback与CFG-DAgger：配对被替换的策略片段与人类修正动作，提供正负监督信号；
4. 工程与系统架构：采用统一末端接口适配异构本体，使用异步动作块合并平滑推理延迟，并构建事件驱动智能体实现规划重估与条件恢复。

1. 仿真表现：RoboTwin 2.0达到93.6%成功率，RoboDojo VLA赛道排名第五；
2. 真机表现：在相同HG-DAgger后训练配置下，三项真机任务表现超越π_0.5；
3. 高难度任务：以太网插入任务中取得70%成功率与0.90进度分；
4. 定性效果：成功实现跨任务事件检索与非预期扰动下的状态自主恢复。
AI.conclusion: MR0通过大规模多模态跨本体数据预训练、流匹配连续控制表征，以及创新的Rollback人机交互修正机制，成功构建了一个具备高精度操作、平滑执行与异常恢复能力的桌面操作具身基座模型系统。
AI.translation: 我们推出了Meituan-Robotics-0（MR0），这是一款面向固定基座桌面操作的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）基座模型与具身智能体系统。MR0结合了1.47亿条视觉-语言样本以及跨12种本体的15,060小时精选机器人轨迹。其三阶段训练方案通过离散动作标记预训练将多模态表征与机器人行为对齐，通过流匹配（flow-matching）中程训练将这些先验迁移至连续跨本体控制，并通过真机后训练对策略进行适配。我们提出了Rollback机制，将替换的策略片段与人类纠正相结合，无需价值学习或优势标注即可为CFG-DAgger提供正负监督。统一的末端执行器接口支持异构本体，而异步动作块合并机制在推理延迟波动的条件下保持动作平滑执行。事件驱动智能体维护持久的任务事件，并在进度或可行性发生变化时重新评估规划，从而实现跨任务检索和条件任务恢复。MR0在RoboTwin 2.0上取得了93.6%的成功率，在RoboDojo VLA赛道中排名第五。在同等条件的HG-DAgger后训练下，MR0在三个真机任务上的平均成功率和进度得分均高于π_0.5。在以太网插线任务中，使用Rollback数据训练的CFG-DAgger达到了70%的成功率和0.90的进度得分。定性智能体部署展现了跨任务事件检索以及从暂时不满足的任务条件中恢复的能力。
AI.summary: 美团推出了面向桌面操作的视觉-语言-动作基座模型Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0)。该模型结合海量多模态与跨本体机器人数据，采用三阶段递进式训练与流匹配技术，并提出Rollback机制优化正负样本模仿学习。结合异步动作执行和事件驱动系统，MR0在多项仿真与真机测试中展现出卓越的操控精度与自愈恢复能力。
AI.keywords: 视觉-语言-动作模型 (VLA), 桌面操作, 具身智能, 流匹配, 模仿学习
AI.comments: 该研究代表了具身智能在工业级应用与基座模型构建方面的重要进展。其创新性在于：1）提出了结合离散预训练与流匹配连续控制的三阶段训练体系；2）Rollback机制巧妙将人类干预片段转化为正负监督信号，绕开了强化学习复杂的价值网络学习；3）异步动作块合并与事件驱动架构较好地兼顾了实际部署中的推理时延与长程任务韧性。局限性在于目前实验与架构主要面向固定底座的桌面级操作，尚未拓展至移动操作或多指灵巧手等更广义场景。

title: Fibered Separation Logic: Weakest Preconditions, Universal Constructions, and Local Independence
summary:
This paper introduces a categorical framework for models of higher-order separation logic including the weakest precondition modality. Weakest preconditions are interpreted by strong monads on a category fibered over a model of Moggi's computational lambda calculus. The fibered categories in question are termed bunched fibrations and shown to be equivalent to BI hyperdoctrines.
  Well-known heuristic techniques for obtaining weakest preconditions are shown to be expressible in categorical terms and are proved sound. The ``baking in the frame rule'' trick is shown to satisfy a universal property. Constructions are given for extending a program logic with cost credits. Our largest case study is parametrized by a category having local independent product (LIP) structure, a notion due to Simpson that axiomatizes name generation, randomness, and local state. From an LIP category, we construct an allocation monad, a bunched fibration, and a monad lifting. We instantiate our construction to obtain a novel probabilistic separation logic for measure-theoretic probability that both simplifies and clarifies prior work.

AI.title_translation: 纤维化分离逻辑：最弱前置条件、泛构造与局部独立性
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个基于束状纤维化和强单子的高阶分离逻辑范畴学框架，泛化并证明了最弱前置条件构造，并据此构建了新型测度论概率分离逻辑。
AI.motivation: 为包含最弱前置条件模态的高阶分离逻辑建立统一、严谨的范畴学语义框架，形式化并验证常用启发式技巧（如内嵌框架规则），以模块化方式支撑名字生成、局部状态和概率等高级特性的建模。
AI.method: 利用纤维化在Moggi计算lambda演算模型上的范畴（束状纤维化，等价于BI超学说）上的强单子解释最弱前置条件；用泛性质形式化启发式规则并支持成本积分扩展；利用局部独立积（LIP）范畴构造分配单子、纤维化结构及单子提升。
AI.result: 证明了束状纤维化与BI超学说等价；证明了最弱前置条件启发式技巧的可靠性及其泛性质；成功构造出用于测度论概率的新型概率分离逻辑，显著简化并阐明了既有成果。
AI.conclusion: 该范畴学框架为研究和设计带最弱前置条件的高阶分离逻辑提供了坚实且模块化的数学基础，能有效简化复杂领域（如测度论概率程序验证）的逻辑构建。
AI.translation: 本文介绍了一个用于包含最弱前置条件模态的高阶分离逻辑模型的范畴学框架。最弱前置条件由纤维化在 Moggi 计算 lambda 演算模型之上的范畴上的强单子来解释。所涉及的纤维化范畴被称为束状纤维化（bunched fibrations），并被证明等价于 BI 超学说。本文证明了用于获取最弱前置条件的知名启发式技术可以用范畴学术语表达并且是可靠的。“内嵌框架规则”（baking in the frame rule）这一技巧被证明满足某个泛性质。本文还给出了用于为程序逻辑扩展成本积分（cost credits）的构造。我们最大的案例研究是由具有局部独立积（LIP）结构的范畴进行参数化的，该概念由 Simpson 提出，用于公理化名字生成、随机性和局部状态。从 LIP 范畴出发，我们构造了一个分配单子、一个束状纤维化和一个单子提升。我们实例化了我们的构造，从而获得了一种用于测度论概率的新型概率分离逻辑，该逻辑既简化又阐明了先前的研究工作。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种用于带最弱前置条件的高阶分离逻辑的范畴学框架。作者将最弱前置条件建模为束状纤维化上的强单子，赋予内嵌框架规则等启发式技巧严格的泛性质解释，并基于局部独立积（LIP）构造了新型测度论概率分离逻辑。
AI.keywords: 分离逻辑, 最弱前置条件, 束状纤维化, BI超学说, 局部独立积
AI.comments: 本文的创新与价值在于：1）首次为包含最弱前置条件的高阶分离逻辑建立了模块化的范畴学语义框架，从泛性质角度深刻解释了程序逻辑中常用的“内嵌框架规则”等启发式技巧；2）将抽象的局部独立积（LIP）结构与高级分离逻辑有效结合，直接推导出测度论概率分离逻辑，兼具理论深度与实用表现力。局限性在于理论高度抽象，且摘要中未提及该范畴框架是否已在交互式定理证明器中完成形式化。

title: Proof of the Cordero-Torregrosa Conjecture for Methods with Arbitrary Rules and Its Refinement under Paired Function and Jacobian Evaluations
comments: 58 pages. Substantially revised and expanded version, including a self-contained proof for arbitrary-rule methods and a refinement for paired function and Jacobian evaluations
summary: We study the Cordero--Torregrosa conjecture on the order that can be guaranteed when solving nonlinear systems with prescribed budgets of function and Jacobian evaluations. We consider deterministic, causal, memoryless methods whose rules may be discontinuous, nonmeasurable, or noncomputable. We give an independent proof of a scalar barrier for queries of $f$ and $f'$ by constructing a fixed entire function, a simple root, and a single sequence of initial points that simultaneously exclude every exponent greater than $2^{d-1}$, where $d$ is the maximum number of queries. An exact simulation of vector-valued responses yields the Cordero--Torregrosa inequality $p\le 2^{N_F+N_J-1}$ for function classes containing the analytic test fields. The proof holds for $N_F,N_J\ge 0$, $N_F+N_J\ge 1$, without assuming $N_J\le N_F$; in particular, it covers $N_J>N_F$. Under pairing at the end of the cycle, we obtain the sharper bound $p\le 2^{N_F-s+1}3^{s-1}$, $s=\min\{N_F,N_J\}\ge 1$, without requiring temporal precedence. The proofs use indistinguishable perturbations, kernels of constraints, and a construction that preserves responses while producing a single entire witness. These results are upper bounds on the universal local order of a cycle; they do not establish attainability for every budget.
comment: 58 pages. Substantially revised and expanded version, including a self-contained proof for arbitrary-rule methods and a refinement for paired function and Jacobian evaluations

AI.title_translation: 任意规则算法下Cordero-Torregrosa猜想的证明及其在成对函数与雅可比评估下的细化
AI.tldr: 本文证明了非线性方程组迭代算法收敛阶的Cordero-Torregrosa猜想，放宽了方法规则约束并给出了成对评估下的更紧上界。
AI.motivation: 探究在给定的函数和雅可比矩阵评估预算下，求解非线性方程组时迭代方法所能达到的收敛阶理论极限，验证并拓展Cordero-Torregrosa猜想。
AI.method: 采用不可区分扰动、约束核分析以及构造单一整函数见证的方法，通过构造特定整函数、单根及初始点序列，精确模拟向量值响应，从而证明收敛阶屏障。
AI.result: 证明了标量查询屏障排除任何大于$2^{d-1}$的收敛阶；对于解析函数类确立了不等式$p\le 2^{N_F+N_J-1}$（涵盖$N_J > N_F$情形）；在循环末端成对评估条件下获得了更紧的上界$p\le 2^{N_F-s+1}3^{s-1}$（其中$s=\min\{N_F,N_J\}\ge 1$）。
AI.conclusion: 成功证明了Cordero-Torregrosa猜想在具有任意规则的确定性、因果、无记忆方法下成立，确定了局部收敛阶的普适理论上界，并在成对评估情形下获得了进一步细化的紧界。
AI.translation: 我们研究了关于在预设的函数与雅可比矩阵评估预算下求解非线性系统所能保证的收敛阶的Cordero--Torregrosa猜想。我们考虑了规则可以是不连续、不可测或不可计算的确定性、因果且无记忆的方法。通过构造一个固定的整函数、单根以及单一初始点序列，我们给出了查询$f$和$f'$标量屏障的独立证明，同时排除了所有大于$2^{d-1}$的指数（其中$d$为最大查询次数）。对向量值响应的精确模拟在包含解析测试场的函数类上导出了Cordero--Torregrosa不等式$p\le 2^{N_F+N_J-1}$。该证明对$N_F,N_J\ge 0$且$N_F+N_J\ge 1$均成立，无需假设$N_J\le N_F$；特别地，它覆盖了$N_J>N_F$的情形。在循环末端成对评估的条件下，我们在不需要时间优先性假设的前提下获得了更紧的界$p\le 2^{N_F-s+1}3^{s-1}$（$s=\min\{N_F,N_J\}\ge 1$）。这些证明利用了不可区分扰动、约束核以及在保留响应的同时生成单个整函数见证的构造法。这些结果是一个循环的通用局部收敛阶的上界；它们并不确立每个预算下的可达性。
AI.summary: 本文研究了非线性方程组求解中收敛阶的理论极限，证明了适用于任意规则（包括不连续或不可计算规则）算法的Cordero-Torregrosa猜想。作者通过构造整函数反例证明了收敛阶上界$p\le 2^{N_F+N_J-1}$对任意非负$N_F, N_J$成立，并在成对评估约束下给出了更为紧致的收敛阶上界。
AI.keywords: Cordero-Torregrosa猜想, 非线性系统, 收敛阶, 雅可比评估, 复杂度上界
AI.comments: 该论文的重要创新在于完全证明了求解非线性系统的Cordero-Torregrosa猜想，不仅放宽了算法规则的限制（允许不连续、不可测或不可计算规则），还打破了以往对雅可比矩阵评估次数不超过函数评估次数的限制（覆盖了$N_J > N_F$的情形）。此外，作者还在成对评估条件下给出了更紧的上界。局限性在于该工作给出的是收敛阶的理论上界，尚未证明所有评估预算下的收敛阶均可达到。

title: Stabilizing Vector Approximate Message Passing with Circuit-Designed Lag-Lead Damping
summary: Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is tuned either manually or adaptively. Using the fact that VAMP iterations are the discretization of an electric circuit, we show that the denoiser and the likelihood act as nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor and damping is a lag filter. This circuit gives a closed-form loop gain whose spectrum can predict when VAMP fails. Because a lag filter cannot isolate the oscillating modes, we add a lead capacitor whose design often results in a negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, our proposed damping strategy achieves a higher convergence rate than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at a lower mean iteration cost. On ill-conditioned multipath channels, across ranks and sparsity levels, it also converges more reliably than existing damping baselines.

AI.title_translation: 基于电路设计超前-滞后阻尼的稳定矢量近似消息传递
AI.tldr: 利用电路建模推导闭式环路增益，并引入带负电容的超前-滞后阻尼，显著提升了VAMP在病态矩阵下的收敛速度与可靠性。
AI.motivation: 矢量近似消息传递（VAMP）算法在面对病态矩阵时经常不收敛，现有的阻尼因子主要依赖手动或自适应调节，且传统滞后滤波无法有效隔离振荡模式。
AI.method: 将VAMP迭代视为电路的离散化过程，把去噪器与似然视为非线性电阻，Onsager校正视为镜像电阻，传统阻尼视为滞后滤波器；基于该电路推导出可预测算法失效的闭式环路增益谱；为解决滞后滤波无法隔离振荡模式的问题，额外设计并引入了一个超前电容（通常表现为负电容），形成电路设计的超前-滞后阻尼策略。
AI.result: 在多种条件数下，该策略以更低的平均迭代成本取得了优于自适应阻尼和安德森加速（Anderson acceleration）的收敛速度；在各种秩和稀疏度水平的病态多径信道上，其收敛可靠性也显著优于现有基线阻尼方法。
AI.conclusion: 通过电路视角的建模和超前-滞后阻尼（引入负电容）设计，能够有效预测并抑制VAMP在病态条件下的振荡模式，显著提升了算法在病态矩阵与信道估计中的收敛速度与可靠性。
AI.translation: 矢量近似消息传递（VAMP）在病态矩阵上往往无法收敛，其阻尼因子通常采用手动或自适应方式进行调节。利用VAMP迭代是电路离散化这一事实，我们证明了去噪器和似然的作用相当于非线性电阻，Onsager校正是镜像电阻，阻尼则是滞后滤波器。该电路提供了闭式环路增益，其频谱可用于预测VAMP何时失效。由于滞后滤波器无法隔离振荡模式，我们加入了一个超前电容，其设计通常会产生负电容。在广泛的条件数范围内，我们提出的阻尼策略以更低的平均迭代成本实现了比自适应阻尼和安德森加速更高的收敛速度。在病态多径信道上，无论秩和稀疏度水平如何，它都比现有的阻尼基线收敛得更加可靠。
AI.summary: 本研究针对VAMP在病态矩阵下易发散的问题，建立其对应的等效电路模型，并基于闭式环路增益谱分析其不稳定性。研究指出传统阻尼仅相当于滞后滤波器，进而通过引入超前电容设计出超前-滞后阻尼方案。实验表明该方法能以更低的迭代开销和更高的可靠性解决病态多径信道及高条件数场景下的收敛问题。
AI.keywords: 矢量近似消息传递 (VAMP), 超前-滞后阻尼, 电路建模, 负电容, 病态矩阵
AI.comments: 该论文将算法迭代动力学映射为模拟电路系统，从控制与电路理论（超前-滞后补偿、负电容设计）的角度深入分析并解决VAMP在病态矩阵下的发散问题。这种交叉视角的建模不仅极具物理与系统直觉，还提供了可预测算法失效的闭式环路增益工具，对消息传递算法的收敛性优化具有启发意义。

title: PathXAI: Evidence-guided structured pathology reporting by transferable tissue segmentation
comments: More experimental results will be added in the future version
summary: Pathology reporting translates tissue observations across regions and slides into diagnoses and supporting morphological descriptions, yet explicit tissue-composition measurements are rarely used to guide H&E-based report generation. We developed PathXAI, which pairs transferable tissue segmentation with a pretrained vision-language model. Because supplying tissue information directly with H&E images gave limited benefit, PathXAI-Report uses segmentation overlays and tissue statistics in separate steps, selects between candidate diagnoses by fixed rules, acquires further images when evidence is insufficient and records every step for review, without updating model weights. Its segmentation component exceeded baselines in mean Dice on internal and external tests. In automated evaluation on 1,200 public and 151 private cases, PathXAI achieved higher agreement with reference diagnoses and documented morphology than H&E-based comparators. On the public cohort, it exceeded Qwen+H&E by 4.4 percentage points in cancer family match rate and 5.7 percentage points in finding F1.
comment: More experimental results will be added in the future version

AI.title_translation: PathXAI：基于可迁移组织分割的证据引导结构化病理报告生成系统
AI.tldr: PathXAI通过多步骤引入可迁移组织分割与统计证据，无需更新模型权重即可显著提升多模态病理报告生成的诊断及形态学描述准确率。
AI.motivation: 病理报告需要将多区域和多切片的组织观察转化为诊断及支持性的形态描述，但显式的组织成分测量很少被直接用于指导基于H&E染色的报告生成，且直接同时输入组织信息和H&E图像带来的提升有限。
AI.method: 开发了PathXAI系统，将可迁移组织分割与预训练视觉语言模型相结合。PathXAI-Report在无需更新模型权重的情况下，在独立步骤中利用分割覆盖层和组织统计数据，采用固定规则在候选诊断中筛选，在证据不足时主动获取更多图像，并完整记录每一步推理以供审查。
AI.result: 分割组件在内部和外部测试中的平均Dice值均优于基线；在1200例公开病例和151例私有病例的自动化评估中，PathXAI在参考诊断和形态学记录上的一致性均高于单纯基于H&E的对照方法；在公开队列中，其癌种家族匹配率和病变发现F1值分别比Qwen+H&E高出4.4和5.7个百分点。
AI.conclusion: PathXAI通过引入可迁移的组织分割与显式证据引导工作流，能够有效提升自动化病理报告生成的诊断准确性和形态学一致性，并提供了可追溯审查的临床潜力。
AI.translation: 病理报告将跨区域和切片的组织观察结果转化为诊断结果及支持性的形态学描述，然而显式的组织成分测量却鲜少被用于指导基于H&E染色的报告生成。我们开发了PathXAI，它将可迁移的组织分割技术与预训练视觉语言模型相结合。由于直接随H&E图像提供组织信息所带来的收益有限，PathXAI-Report在独立步骤中分别使用分割覆盖图和组织统计数据，依据固定规则在候选诊断中进行选择，在证据不足时获取更多图像，并在无需更新模型权重的情况下记录每一步以供审查。其分割组件在内部和外部测试的平均Dice指标上均超越了基准线。在涵盖1200例公开病例和151例私有病例的自动化评估中，PathXAI与参考诊断及记录形态学的一致性均高于基于H&E的对照方法。在公开队列中，其癌种家族匹配率和发现F1分数分别比Qwen+H&E高出4.4和5.7个百分点。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了PathXAI，一个结合可迁移组织分割与预训练视觉语言模型的病理报告生成系统。针对直接融合组织信息与H&E图像收益有限的问题，PathXAI-Report分步利用分割覆盖与统计信息，依规则筛选诊断并在证据不足时调取新图像，全流程可审查且无需微调模型权重。实验表明，该方法在分割性能、诊断匹配率及形态学描述准确性上均显著优于现有基线。
AI.keywords: 病理报告生成, 组织分割, 视觉语言模型, 可解释性, 证据引导
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地将可迁移的组织分割信息与视觉语言模型解耦为多步骤的证据引导工作流，无需微调模型权重即可动态调用更多证据并保留完整推理过程，极大提升了病理报告的可解释性与临床可靠性。其局限在于目前测试规模仍偏自动化评估，临床病理专家的实际读片交互与评估效果有待进一步验证。

title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
comments: Abstract shortened due to arxiv requirements
summary:
We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial.
  The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $ε$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $ε$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/ε$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set. In this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(ε)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/ε^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis.
  On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.
