title: Stability Analysis of Single- and Multi-Snapshot ESPRIT
summary: Spectral estimation seeks to recover unknown frequencies from $T$ snapshots, each consisting of $Ω+1$ noisy Fourier measurements. Super-resolution refers to the recovery of frequencies whose minimum separation $Δ$ is smaller than $1/Ω$. We establish state-of-the-art stability bounds for single- and multi-snapshot ESPRIT when the frequencies form well-separated clumps, with the largest clump containing $n^\star$ frequencies. In particular, for single-snapshot ESPRIT, our error bound scales as $$ \mathcal{O}(Ω^{-1}\mathrm{SRF}^{2n^\star-2}\cdot\mathrm{Noise}), $$ where $\mathrm{SRF}:=(ΩΔ)^{-1}$ denotes the super-resolution factor, provided that the noise level satisfies $\mathrm{Noise}\lesssim(ΩΔ)^{2n^\star-2}$. In comparison with the minimax bounds [arXiv:1904.09186] and the computational resolution limits [arXiv:2003.02917, arXiv:2211.15208], our result shows that single-snapshot ESPRIT achieves the optimal stability scaling in the super-resolution regime. For multi-snapshot ESPRIT, we establish error bounds under both deterministic noise and Gaussian white noise, attaining the best-known SRF dependence under weaker conditions. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical error bounds.

title: Residual-Closed-Loop SAGE-Brent Estimation for Unknown-Order Wideband Underwater Acoustic Channels
comments: 31 pages, 14 figures, 9 tables. Includes supplementary materials (Tables S1-S5)
summary: Grid mismatch in wideband channel estimation leaves structured cancellation residuals after strong-path subtraction. These residuals generate spurious correlation peaks or mask weak arrivals, turning continuous parameter errors into path-count errors. We propose RC-SAGE-Brent, a residual-closed-loop estimator that jointly refines continuous delay-scale parameters and corrects the unknown-order path set. Within each feedback cycle, ambiguity-constrained alternating Brent searches suppress strong-path cancellation residuals. Candidate validation, resolution-constrained pruning, and full-domain residual redetection then revise the active path set. For linear frequency modulation (LFM) probes, an observable signal-to-residual ratio adaptively scales the model-order penalty to mitigate overestimation caused by delay-scale coupling. Theoretical analysis links off-grid parameter errors to local cancellation-residual curvature and weak-path detectability. Factorial ablations, paired comparisons against standard sparse and off-grid estimators, and measured channel replay demonstrate improved path-set recovery and waveform reconstruction while delineating the operational boundaries of the method.
comment: 31 pages, 14 figures, 9 tables. Includes supplementary materials (Tables S1-S5)

title: RaGCD: Reliability-Aware 2D-3D Multimodal Generalized Category Discovery
summary: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to recognize known categories while discovering novel ones from partially labeled data. Existing GCD studies primarily focus on unimodal observations or image-text interactions, leaving the complementarity between visual appearance and explicit 3D geometry underexplored. To exploit complementary visual appearance and spatial geometry, we investigate GCD with paired images and point clouds. However, the relative reliability of these modalities varies across samples, so unreliable evidence can compromise both multimodal fusion and cross-modal knowledge transfer. This challenge is particularly pronounced for novel categories, where labeled supervision is unavailable. To address it, we propose RaGCD, a reliability-aware framework for 2D-3D multimodal GCD. Specifically, Reliability-aware Modality Allocation (RMA) combines prediction-derived reliability cues with modality-specific features to adaptively allocate image and point-cloud contributions at the channel level. Reliability-conditioned Alignment (RCA) further reweights feature-level and prediction-level alignment and selects reliable observations for prototype-level alignment, regulating cross-modal interaction according to sample reliability. Extensive experiments on ModelNet40, Washington RGB-D, and ShapeNet-ViPC demonstrate that RaGCD outperforms the compared methods in overall and novel-category clustering accuracy. Ablation studies support the complementary roles of RMA and RCA, while controlled corruption experiments show that modality allocation shifts toward the less corrupted modality. These results support the effectiveness of reliability-aware interaction for category discovery from paired appearance and geometry.

title: A Faster and Efficient Indoor User Localization Using Bistatic MIMO Radar
summary: Indoor user localization is essential for applications such as asset tracking, robotic navigation, and smart-building automation where satellite-based positioning is unavailable. Bistatic MIMO radar exploits bistatic range measurements and geometric diversity from distributed antennas, but low-SNR conditions make the resulting estimation ill-conditioned. We formulate indoor localization as a Tikhonov-regularized nonlinear least-squares problem and solve it with a damped Gauss-Newton (DGN) algorithm, in which each iteration reduces to a closed-form 3x3 linear solve followed by an Armijo backtracking line search. Simulations show accuracy on par with, and runtime far faster than, an SDP-based benchmark.

title: DialInstruct-TTS: Interactive Expressive Speech Generation via Multi-Turn Dialogue with Fine-Grained Temporal Control
summary: Existing instruction-based TTS systems primarily support one-shot, utterance-level control, where a single instruction determines the speaking style of an entire utterance. As a result, even minor refinements require rewriting the instruction and regenerating the full utterance, limiting fine-grained interactive control. We propose DialInstruct-TTS, an interactive multi-turn expressive TTS framework that enables users to iteratively refine generated speech through natural-language dialogue until the desired style is achieved. At each dialogue turn, a Qwen-based planner integrates the dialogue history and latest user instruction into a complete TemporalPlan, while a temporal acoustic control module provides fine-grained control over emotion, speaking rate, volume, and phonation. Reference-latent revision preserves non-target regions across turns, allowing users to modify only the requested attributes or temporal spans while retaining previously satisfactory speech. Subjective evaluations demonstrate improved global instruction following, accurate local style realization, and effective non-target preservation. Compared with conventional one-shot interaction requiring full instruction restatement and utterance regeneration, DialInstruct-TTS substantially improves perceived convenience and interaction comfort. Audio samples are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/w/eacl-demo-17C5/.

title: Application of the Phase Correction Method in Tracking Modules of Navigation Receivers
comments: 15 pages, 17 figures. The paper is accepted for publication in the journal "Radiotechnika" (Radio engineering)
summary: One of the problems of the tracking modules is their significant inertia in case of narrow bandwidth, which is desirable to mitigate signal noise. The paper describes a method of phase correction, improving accuracy and dynamic characteristics of the tracking process in GNSS receivers. The pivotal idea of the method supposes correction of the phase deviation between the received signal and its local copy at the end of every integration period. This correction is performed directly over the phase accumulator of a DDS system. This approach reduces inertial effects crucially. Application of phase correction method with narrow filter bandwidth is much more efficient when FLL-assisted PLL tracking is used. It is shown that in this case a separate FLL discriminator is not needed, and the resulting filter structure can be significantly simplified.
comment: 15 pages, 17 figures. The paper is accepted for publication in the journal "Radiotechnika" (Radio engineering)

title: Passive ladder-network representation of the radiation impedance of a spherical cap on a rigid sphere
comments: 13 pages (preprint format), 3 figures. Submitted to JASA Express Letters
summary: A loudspeaker in a closed box is modeled as a rigid sphere with an axially moving cap. For an axisymmetric cone-velocity profile, its radiation impedance is written as a network. Each spherical-harmonic mode has an impedance rational in frequency, realized exactly as a finite passive ladder of masses and compliances terminated in a resistance. Ideal transformers set by Legendre coefficients couple these ladders; truncated modes reduce to a residual mass. Despite the different geometry, the impedance resembles that of a baffled piston but, at equal volume velocity, has half its low-frequency resistance and about three quarters of its radiation mass.
comment: 13 pages (preprint format), 3 figures. Submitted to JASA Express Letters

title: ESDCodec: Ultra-Low Bitrate Speech Codec with Enhanced Semantic Disentanglement and Subband Decoding
summary: Despite recent advances in neural speech codecs, achieving highfidelity speech reconstruction at low bitrates remains a formidable challenge. To address this limitation, we propose ESDCodec, a speech codec that integrates a thoroughly enhanced semantic quantizer and a conditioned decoder network. Specifically, we employ a randomly initialized and frozen codebook, followed by a lightweight projector, to encode semantic details entirely within a linear space while enhancing codebook utilization. To further improve perceptual quality, we design a condition network that explicitly injects prior subband knowledge into the upsampling decoder. Taking the de-quantized feature as input, this network predicts subband signals, thereby providing fine-grained guidance for waveform reconstruction. Extensive experimental results show that ESDCodec achieves superior reconstruction performance at an ultra-low bitrate of 0.85kbps. For LLM-based speech generation tasks, ESDCodec also consistently outperforms existing codec models.

title: Finite Blocklength Performance Analysis of Uplink RSMA with Practical Imperfections
summary: Future generations of wireless networks will support massive communication and hyper-reliable low-latency communications, which are fundamental to large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) deployments with stringent performance requirements. To support such diverse and demanding requirements, robust and flexible multiple access schemes are essential. In this work, we develop a comprehensive analytical framework for evaluating uplink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) in the finite blocklength regime under realistic non-ideal conditions. Specifically, we derive closed-form expressions for the block error rate (BLER) and goodput, accounting for imperfect channel state information at the receiver (CSIR), imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC), and hardware impairments. To reflect practical wireless environments, we model the channel using Nakagami-m fading model. Our analysis shows that at lower transmit power levels, imperfect CSIR is the dominant performance-limiting factor, whereas hardware impairments and imperfect SIC become more significant in degrading system performance as the transmit power increases. To further understand the system behavior, we derive asymptotic BLER expressions. We also analyze the impact of rate allocation, demonstrating its critical role in ensuring fairness and reliability. Monte Carlo simulations validate our analytical expressions. Notably, our results show that uplink RSMA significantly outperforms NOMA even when RSMA operates under harsh imperfect CSIR. This superiority establishes RSMA as a robust and efficient candidate for future wireless networks in practical, constrained environments

title: Dual-Parabola Interpolator: A Low-Bias Peak Estimator for Distributed Radar Synchronization
comments: 6 pages, 7 figures. Submitted for peer review as a conference paper
summary: Coherent distributed radar processing requires accurate wireless synchronization. Two-way time transfer (TWTT) obtains reception timestamps from sampled matched-filter peaks, but interpolation bias limits accuracy even when noise is reduced by higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or averaging. Three-point parabolic interpolation is attractive for its simple, explicit formula; reducing its bias generally requires more elaborate fitting, such as higher-order polynomials, or a model tailored to a particular peak shape. A practical alternative should retain this simplicity and interpretability while approaching the low bias of more flexible fits. We propose the Dual-Parabola Interpolator (DPI), which combines two parabolic estimates from five amplitude samples near the matched-filter peak. An adaptive weight cancels the leading interpolation error without requiring a waveform-specific peak model or a correction table. Simulations over flat and standardized multipath channels show bias comparable to a five-point quartic fit, with essentially the same standard deviation as the other interpolators and an execution cost close to a three-point parabolic fit. This combination is useful for TWTT in urban or other multipath settings, where channel distortion prevents reliance on a nominal peak shape.
comment: 6 pages, 7 figures. Submitted for peer review as a conference paper

title: CFAR Detection on Non-Coherently Integrated Angular Maps for mmWave Radio SLAM
comments: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Reliable multipath detection is essential for millimeter-wave simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), where propagation paths reflecting off the environment provide geometric constraints beyond the dominant line-of-sight component. This paper develops constant false alarm rate (CFAR)-based detectors for beam-swept bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Starting from conventional CFAR on the I/Q datacube, we derive a modified detector for non-coherently integrated angular power maps, where the post-integration noise statistics differ from those assumed by standard cell-averaging CFAR. To improve practicality, we introduce a multi-cell cell-under-test formulation and a plus-shaped training window that reduces computational cost while accounting for sidelobe structure. The proposed methods are evaluated on experimental 60 GHz indoor measurements using a snapshot-SLAM estimator. Compared with a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based detector, the proposed CFAR approaches reduce the overall positioning RMSE from 0.30 m to 0.24-0.26 m, with the largest improvement in non-line-of-sight snapshots. The multi-cell non-coherent detector further lowers the computational complexity without degrading positioning accuracy, demonstrating its suitability for practical multipath radio-SLAM.
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

title: Spectral-Domain Information Geometry of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian and Elliptical Extensions
summary:
This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard $L^2$ inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher--Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices.
  We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered $L^2$ geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.

title: Edge-AI for Heart Murmur Screening in Low-Resource Settings
summary: Early and reliable detection of heart murmurs is essential for the timely diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases, yet traditional auscultation remains subjective and dependent on expert interpretation. This work investigates an artificial intelligence (AI)-based approach for heart murmur detection using the CirCor Heart Sound dataset, with a particular focus on deployment in low-cost and resource-constrained embedded platforms. A lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) is developed using spectrogram features extracted from heart sound recordings. The complete processing pipeline, from feature extraction to final prediction, is implemented and validated on an STM32F401 microcontroller (MCU). To enable real-time execution within the limited hardware resources of the target platform, memory- and latency-oriented optimizations together with fixed-point processing are employed. Experimental results demonstrate that accurate murmur detection can be achieved despite the severe computational constraints of the embedded device. The proposed system achieves a patient-level accuracy of 92.5% and an F1-score above 82.5%, while using far fewer parameters than conventional high-resource deep-learning approaches. The embedded implementation exhibits only marginal performance degradation, with performance drops below 2 percentage points compared to the original full-precision implementation. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of real-time AI-based heart murmur screening on low-cost microcontrollers. By reducing hardware requirements while preserving predictive performance, the proposed approach can facilitate the development of portable, affordable, and widely deployable diagnostic tools for remote and resource-limited healthcare settings.

title: Sensing-Constrained Diversity-Multiplexing Tradeoff in MIMO ISAC: A Geometric Approach
comments: Accepted for presentation at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026
summary: Diversity and multiplexing are the two fundamental gains of multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) communications, enabling systems to simultaneously achieve increased reliability and higher data rates. The intricate interplay between these two metrics is captured by the celebrated diversity-multiplexing tradeoff (DMT). With the rapid evolution of wireless technologies, low-latency integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a key enabler for 6G applications, including extended reality (XR) and massive digital twins. Consequently, understanding the DMT within MIMO ISAC systems becomes critical. In this paper, we investigate the communication DMT in a mono-static MIMO ISAC system under Rayleigh fading, specifically when the transmitter is constrained to emit sensing-optimal waveforms. By unveiling the geometric properties of generalized Stiefel manifolds and employing large-deviation analysis, we characterize the asymptotic outage probability of this typical ISAC channel. This formulation yields an elegant converse bound on the sensing-constrained DMT. Ultimately, our work provides an answer to a pivotal unanswered question in ISAC system design: How much MIMO gain is fundamentally sacrificed in communication to integrate optimal sensing capabilities?
comment: Accepted for presentation at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026

title: One-hot Coding-based URA with RFFI-Enabled Message Authentication
comments: 5 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE Journal
summary: Unsourced random access (URA) has emerged as a promising paradigm for enabling massive connectivity in Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks. However, since URA transmissions do not contain device identifiers, the receiver may not associate decoded messages with their originating devices, introducing a security vulnerability: forged messages may be decoded as legitimate. To address this problem, this paper proposes a one-hot coding (OHC)-based URA framework that enables message authentication while preserving the unsourced transmission principle. Specifically, distinct messages are mapped onto orthogonal channel uses via an OHC-based common codebook and transmitted using on-off keying modulation. The resulting orthogonal channel structure enables radio-frequency fingerprint identification to authenticate received signals by exploiting device-specific hardware impairments, thereby authenticating decoded messages without introducing an additional authentication payload. Analytical expressions for the per-user probability of error and the probability of successful spoofing are derived. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme enables secure URA transmission while maintaining reliable communication performance in ultra-short-payload IoT scenarios.
comment: 5 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE Journal

title: Impulse Response Estimation via Laguerre-Fourier Expansion
summary: The empirical transfer function estimate (ETFE) is a widely used method for system identification of linear time-invariant (LTI) systems in engineering disciplines such as acoustics, audio engineering, seismography, and tomography. However, ETFE suffers from numerical limitations when the excitation signal is band-limited or vanishes at certain frequencies, which is a common physical constraint of the excitation in practice. In such cases, division in the frequency domain becomes heavily ill-conditioned, and small measurement disturbances or numerical inaccuracies can degrade the solution. This paper presents L-ETFE, a generalization of ETFE based on Laguerre-Fourier expansions that addresses these limitations. After a suitable transformation, the method can yield a well-conditioned circulant problem even when the original ETFE system is ill-conditioned. Solving this problem via classical ETFE yields the discrete Laguerre-Fourier coefficients of the system's transfer function. The desired impulse response (IR) of the system-to-be-identified can then be recovered by a subsequent transformation pipeline. We derive novel and efficient algorithms for performing these transformations and analyse the conditioning of the transformed problem, explicitly characterizing its dependence on the input and a parameter used in the Laguerre-Fourier expansion. We evaluate the method on two simulated discrete-time LTI systems of varying complexity. The experiments demonstrate accurate IR recovery for spectral-zero and band-limited excitation, where standard ETFE fails.

title: Manifold-Constrained PET Reconstruction with Learned Flow-Matching Priors
summary: Image reconstruction for positron emission tomography (PET) is an ill-posed Poisson inverse problem. In this work, we introduce an unsupervised, optimization-based reconstruction framework that employs a flow-matching generative model as a learned manifold prior. We train the generative model on high-quality PET images to learn a differentiable ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based transport from a Gaussian latent distribution to the PET image distribution. We incorporate this generator as an explicit manifold constraint into a regularized Poisson likelihood formulation. To solve the resulting problem, we develop an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm that integrates an expectation-maximization (EM)-type surrogate update for Poisson data fidelity with gradient-based latent-space optimization. Numerical simulations and in vivo PET experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy compared with conventional reconstruction methods and recent deep learning-based approaches, particularly in low-count settings, with competitive computational efficiency.

title: PRIMO: GPU-Accelerated Joint Beamforming and RIS Placement Optimization for Outdoor-to-Indoor Coverage at FR1(C) and FR3
comments: 5 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Presented at the 2026 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers, Pacific Grove, CA, USA, Oct. 25-28, 2026
summary: Upper mid-band spectrum is promising for 5G and 6G cellular networks, yet concrete and low-emissivity glass impose over 20 dB of building penetration loss above 2 GHz, degrading outdoor-to-indoor (O2I) coverage. A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) on a neighboring building bypasses this blockage by focusing energy onto indoor users. This paper introduces PRIMO (Parallel RIS Min-Rate Optimization), a training-free joint optimizer of base-station precoding, RIS phase shifts, and RIS placement, validated by calibrated ray tracing in a MetroTech Commons digital twin (Brooklyn, NY) at 6.75 and 16.95 GHz. At equal physical aperture, half-wavelength spacing packs 6.25 times as many elements per array at FR3 as at FR1(C), so FR1(C) leads at low indoor-user counts while FR3 dominates at higher counts, where the additional spatial degrees of freedom suppress inter-user interference. Above a 1 bps/Hz service floor, PRIMO supports 92% more indoor users at FR3 than at FR1(C), and raises the minimum user rate by up to 90% over a fully converged alternating-optimization baseline while running about 100 times faster.
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Presented at the 2026 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers, Pacific Grove, CA, USA, Oct. 25-28, 2026

title: Wideband Channel Measurements in the Lower FR3 Band (6-12 GHz) for Industrial Environments
summary: The upper mid-band, also known as Frequency Range 3 (FR3), spans 7.125-24.25 GHz and is a key candidate band for sixth-generation (6G) wireless communications. However, channel measurements in industrial environments remain scarce, and the 3GPP indoor-factory (InF) channel model, developed for omnidirectional antennas, has yet to be validated across the FR3 band. This paper presents a wideband channel measurement campaign in an industrial production hall, covering 135 line-of-sight (LOS) positions at 1-18 m and 30 non-line-of-sight (NLOS) positions behind an industrial robot at 2.5-16.5 m across 6-12 GHz. In LOS, the path-loss exponent ranged from 1.87 to 2.12, and the close-in fits agreed with the 3GPP InF-LOS model to within approximately 2 dB. However, shadow fading was only 1.4-1.7 dB, compared with the model's 4.3 dB. In NLOS, the robot caused an excess loss that increased from 10.3 to 13.0 dB between 6.5 and 11.5 GHz, consistent with diffraction. Blocking the direct path raised the mean directional delay spread from approximately 5 to 25 ns, close to omnidirectional values. These results indicate that the 3GPP InF model captures mean LOS path loss well but overestimates the variability of beam-aligned FR3 links, and that blockage loss in FR3 is frequency dependent. The dataset and processing code are publicly available.

title: Denoising Multiuser Interference Enabled Iterative AI Receiver
summary: When interfering users transmit finite-alphabet symbols, the aggregate of multiuser interference and thermal noise in a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receiver is generally non-Gaussian. Its covariance alone does not specify the likelihood required for Bayesian detection. Conventional minimum mean-square error interference rejection combining (MMSE-IRC) is optimal among linear estimators with known second-order statistics, but it does not generally attain the Bayesian MMSE estimate in this setting. In this article, we propose an iterative artificial intelligence (AI) receiver that jointly refines interference cancellation, channel estimation, and desired-user detection. At each iteration, an interference denoising network reconstructs the received interference from the residual observation, covariance information, and uncertainty in the desired-user soft decisions. After cancellation, the preceding soft decisions support successive interference cancellation among desired-user streams and yield least squares (LS) channel estimates at data positions. A channel estimation network refines these estimates using the preceding channel estimate. Finally, MMSE-IRC preprocessing provides an effective channel matrix and soft symbol estimates to a Transformer-ResNet-PIC detector, which produces symbol probabilities for the next iteration. We also relate these structured detector inputs to the likelihood gradient of a relaxed Bayesian detection problem. The resulting receiver uses soft decisions to couple the three processing stages across iterations. Link-level simulations show that denoising multiuser interference enables the proposed iterative AI receiver to approach the attainable theoretical performance bound. The proposed receiver substantially outperforms the conventional quasi-ML receiver based on LMMSE channel estimation and MMSE-IRC preprocessing.

title: Beyond TR 38.811 for 6G NTN Channel Models
summary: As the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) expands 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) to S, Ku, and Ka bands for integration with existing terrestrial cellular networks, the necessary satellite channel model for link and network performance evaluation remains tied to TR 38.811, last revised in 2020. We identify issues on multiple fronts: inappropriate parameter specifications based on very limited site-specific environments considered, omission of satellite-induced Doppler spread and directional antenna effects and lack of a transparent channel model generation procedure. To address these limitations, we re-derive the channel parameters using ray tracing (RT) over urban and rural environments based on ITU-R building statistics. Our results show that TR 38.811 substantially overestimates the K-factor at low elevations and predicts a decreasing trend with elevation, which is inconsistent with RT. The Ka-band clutter loss (CL) also exceeds the RT estimates by more than 15 dB in urban cases. It also underestimates rural delay spread (DS) at low elevations and predicts an elevation trend inconsistent with RT. We further quantify the previously neglected satellite-induced Doppler spread. Finally, we demonstrate that the conventional TR 38.811 channel generator significantly underestimates the K-factor in the presence of directional antenna (beamforming), while our modified generator substantially reduces this discrepancy.

title: Sparse Range-Doppler Profile Recovery in Colored Interference for Adaptive Radar
summary: Range-Doppler profile (RDP) recovery is a fundamental task in adaptive radar signal processing, whose performance can be severely degraded by Doppler grid mismatch and colored interference. This article develops a unified sparsity-aware framework for on-grid and off-grid RDP recovery in the presence of correlated clutter with unknown spectral properties. The problem is formulated within a regularized maximum likelihood framework by exploiting both primary and secondary data, where the sparse RDP and interference covariance are jointly inferred, while Doppler frequency displacements are additionally estimated in the off-grid case to mitigate basis mismatch. Both covariance-adaptive one-step formulations and their sample-covariance-matrix-based two-step alternatives are developed within the mentioned framework. The resulting challenging nonconvex optimization problems are efficiently tackled by a majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm for the on-grid case and an MM-minimum block improvement (MBI) approach for the off-grid counterpart. Furthermore, Bayesian information criterion (BIC)-based refinement strategies are introduced to improve RDP recovery and Doppler frequency displacement estimation. Numerical results under colored interference demonstrate the superior recovery performance of the proposed methods over representative benchmarks.

title: Cross-Spectral Analysis of Bivariate Graph Signals
summary: With the advancements in technology and monitoring tools, we often encounter multivariate graph signals, which can be seen as the realizations of multivariate graph processes, and revealing the relationship between their constituent quantities is one of the important problems. To address this issue, we propose a cross-spectral analysis tool for bivariate graph signals. The main goal of this study is to extend the scope of spectral analysis of graph signals to multivariate graph signals. In this study, we define joint weak stationarity graph processes and introduce graph cross-spectral density and coherence for multivariate graph processes. We propose several estimators for the cross-spectral density and investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed estimators. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed estimators through numerical experiments, including simulation studies and a real data application. Finally, as an interesting extension, we discuss robust spectral analysis of graph signals in the presence of outliers.

title: FDR-Controlled Variable Selection for Generalized Linear Models and Cox Regression with Virtual Dummies
summary: In genomics, imaging and clinical studies, only a few of many candidate predictors are often nonlinearly associated with a response that may be, e.g. binary, categorical, a count or a censored event time. The Terminating-Random Experiments (T-Rex) selector is a scalable variable selection method that controls the false discovery rate (FDR) by letting synthetic null variables (dummies) compete with the real predictors. While the FDR control theory embraces more general settings, to date, the T-Rex selector has been specified only for linear models. We propose a memory-efficient selection procedure with FDR control for generalized linear models and Cox regression by extending the recently developed virtual dummy construction to score-based forward selection for Bernoulli, Poisson, multinomial and Cox responses. The virtual-dummy-based selection path remains equal in distribution to explicit augmentation, so FDR control carries over under the same assumptions. Simulations confirm this equivalence and the power gained by correct model specification. Real-world applicability is illustrated on simulated genotypes and on cancer survival data.

title: Prediction Inference for Hybrid Models on Realized Volatility Forecasting
summary: GARCH-LSTM hybrid models have become increasingly popular in the volatility forecasting literature. To date, these models have almost exclusively focused on point estimation and accuracy measures such as RMSE and MAPE, while failing to assess the uncertainty of these point estimates. We approach this gap in two ways. First, we extend the existing GARCH-LSTM model by modeling the conditional mean with an ARMA structure. Second, we develop a forward bootstrap algorithm to build multi-step-ahead prediction intervals for future realized volatility. In order to address the notorious undercoverage of prediction intervals, we implement two solutions. One draws bootstrap innovations from the empirical residual distribution to mimic the fat-tail property of financial series. The other utilizes principles from conformal prediction to systematically extend the prediction interval length. We evaluate the methods in simulations with heavy-tailed and time-varying GARCH processes and in rolling-window forecasts of four U.S. stock indices from 2020 to 2025. The ARMA-based hybrid gives the lowest point-forecast errors in most settings, and combining both remedies with the mean-based hybrid yields intervals closest to the nominal level among competing methods.

title: Reconciling District Prediction Markets and Seat-Count Buckets in U.S. Midterm Elections
summary: The prediction market platform Kalshi offers individual markets for the winner in each U.S. congressional district and an aggregate market for the total number of Democratic House seats. We develop an applied statistical framework for reconciling these two market layers, since the aggregate seat count is determined by the collection of individual district outcomes. The framework combines a latent-Gaussian dependence structure with a log-odds adjustment to district probabilities and a power adjustment to aggregate seat-count probabilities, with parameters estimated by divergence minimization. Applied to a July 30, 2026 snapshot, the three-parameter primary model achieves close reconciliation, with forward and reverse KL divergences both approximately 0.0013, while yielding a positive latent national correlation, a negative district log-odds shift, and flattening of the aggregate target distribution. Daily analysis of 236 dates from January through August 2026 reveals two relatively stable periods separated by a spring transition period exhibiting substantial volatility in both parameter and divergence values. The framework provides a diagnostic approach for assessing cross-market consistency in hierarchically structured prediction or financial markets.

title: Deceleration without identification: testing a power-law trend in Bitcoin prices under persistent noise
comments: 25 pages, 6 figures. Pre-registered protocol and forecasts: https://osf.io/2rdty. Replication package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23218897
summary: Plotted against time since its first block on logarithmic axes, the price of Bitcoin lies close to a straight line, and a power law in time has been proposed as its long-run trend. A good fit is weak evidence: when deviations from a trend are as persistent as a random walk, regressions on time find trends and high $R^2$ where none exist. We first bound what fifteen years of weekly prices can reveal, then test only what is answerable. Using a few low-frequency averages, invariant to the noise scale and calibrated over a declared family of persistent deviations with a four-year cycle and declining volatility, we test constant drift in expected log price against an added log-age term. The procedure was fixed, validated and publicly hashed before it was applied once. Constant drift is rejected under this family at nominal 5%, and a log-age coefficient of 5.7, close to the published exponent, is not rejected. The rejection does not survive allowing persistence beyond a random walk, and a Gompertz curve with a ceiling fits about as well as the power law. Whether deviations revert to the trend cannot be decided. Registered forecasts for 2027-2030 will be scored by future prices.
comment: 25 pages, 6 figures. Pre-registered protocol and forecasts: https://osf.io/2rdty. Replication package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23218897

title: DynamAuction: A Reinforcement Learning Environment for Repeated Auctions with Dynamic Value
summary: A buyer who repeatedly participates in auctions for related items often faces a dynamic value problem: what they win today changes what tomorrow's items are worth. Despite the empirical importance of such effects, especially in display advertising, the algorithmic literature on repeated auctions has largely focused on the learning problem, by treating each opportunity as a contextual bandit, while sidestepping the planning problem induced by the dependence of current value on past wins. We introduce DynamAuction, a synthetic environment for single-buyer sequential bidding. The reward from each win depends on the buyer's history of previous wins, summarized through a carry-over state. The environment supports first- and second-price auctions, non-homogeneous Poisson arrivals, delayed feedback, saturation, and recency effects. We also introduce a new class of Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithms. On our benchmark scenario, these MPC policies outperform off-the-shelf deep RL baselines (PPO, SAC, TD3) as well as a tuned shading baseline. We release DynamAuction to support RL research on repeated auctions.

title: How much can a human being lift? A Bayesian latent capability model for Olympic weightlifting
summary: Estimates of the limits of human performance are usually built on record books, on the premise that a record is the best an athlete could do. In Olympic weightlifting the premise fails, because the competitor declares the weight before each of three attempts per lift and only the heaviest successful attempt is recorded, so a record is a lower bound, chosen by the athlete, on a maximal capability never observed. We treat the maximal lift of each competitor on each competition day as a latent variable, of which every attempt is a trial and every declared weight a measurement. Its distribution at a given bodyweight follows an extreme value mixture model with an estimated threshold, and an athlete-specific random effect links the competitions of each athlete. The model is fitted to the 117,892 attempts of 5,040 athletes in 141 international competitions between 2017 and 2026. The upper tail of capability is bounded, with posterior probability above 0.999 for men, 0.96 for the women's snatch and 0.94 for the women's clean and jerk. At 110 kilograms of bodyweight the men's ceiling lies one to three per cent above the heaviest lifts, against twelve and sixteen per cent for women at 86 kilograms. The record book alone places the men's ceiling six and twelve kilograms higher, because the best lift of a day ending on a success overstates capability.

title: Probabilistic Upscaling of the Interfacial Transition Zone Behaviour in Concrete
summary: The stiffness and cracking behaviour of concrete are influenced by the interfacial transition zone (ITZ), the thin shell of paste that surrounds each aggregate. Yet the ITZ's mechanical properties are poorly characterized and are usually assigned to mesoscale models through ad hoc reduction factors. Because the ITZ is only tens of micrometres thick, its stiffness must be inferred indirectly from micromechanical tests, and the resulting estimates vary widely between studies and are rarely reported with a quantified uncertainty. We present a workflow that calibrates a homogenized ITZ model against the surface displacements of several micro-cantilever bending specimens and returns its stiffness descriptors as posterior distributions rather than single values. The calibration is posed as a Bayesian inverse problem with a model-discrepancy term, sampled with a surrogate-assisted Bouncy Particle sampler, the first application of this sampler to a real-world engineering problem. We compare a pooled model, which fits one descriptor vector to all specimens, with a hierarchical model that treats the specimens as draws from a common population and is sampled with a local extension of the sampler. The hierarchical model separates the estimation uncertainty from the aggregate-to-aggregate material variability, where only the former shrinks as more data are added. Propagated through a representative volume element of several aggregates, its predictive yields broader distributions of the mesoscale stress and strain and a wider spread variety of maximum von Mises stress locations. The calibration places the ITZ thickness above the 30 μm to 80 μm commonly assumed in the literature.

title: Global Trends and Heterogeneity in Modified Adjusted Net Savings
summary: Modified adjusted net savings is a derived weak sustainability indicator obtained by subtracting education expenditure from adjusted net savings (ANS). Because ANS equals net national savings plus education expenditure minus natural-resource depletion and carbon dioxide damage, MANS isolates the savings and depletion components and is useful when education expenditure would otherwise dominate cross-country comparisons. This study documents the global distribution, long-run trends, and cross-country heterogeneity of MANS excluding particulate emission damage over 1990-2021. The accounting base is the World Bank World Development Indicators series NY.ADJ.SVNX.CD, and MANS is constructed by subtracting education expenditure from this series. We combine global maps, aggregate time series, country-level heatmaps, distributional statistics, and income group comparisons. The results show that global MANS has increased substantially in aggregate, but its evolution as a share of nominal GDP has been more volatile and uneven across countries. Per capita MANS and global MANS totals remain concentrated in high-income and large economies, whereas low-income and lower-middle-income groups display persistently lower and more volatile outcomes. Country rankings are highly persistent, and some populous countries exhibit pronounced fluctuations associated with natural-resource dependence and structural change. The study provides a reproducible descriptive benchmark for monitoring sustainable development and highlights the need to interpret MANS in current US dollars alongside income-group and country-specific contexts. The findings are relevant for macroeconomic policy, natural-capital accounting, and the design of sustainability-oriented investment strategies.

title: Causal Learning with Invalid Instruments for High-dimensional Imaging Responses
summary: Large-scale neuroimaging studies provide high-dimensional imaging phenotypes for understanding brain-related diseases and their causal relations with biological risk factors. While instrumental variable (IV) methods can address unmeasured confounding in such observational data, existing IV methods face significant limitations when applied to high-dimensional imaging data, particularly in handling large-scale data and leveraging the intrinsic spatial structure of images. To address these challenges, we propose High-dimensional Functional-imaging Instrumental Variable Estimation (Hi-FIVE), a novel framework for estimating spatially varying causal effects when a majority of the candidate instruments may be locally invalid. We first establish identifiability conditions under which the spatial continuity of the causal effect surface propagates identification from regions where valid instruments form a plurality into regions where they do not, provided that invalid-IV effects switch on non-smoothly. Motivated by this result, Hi-FIVE combines penalized multivariate splines over triangulations for the causal surface and region-wise penalties for spatially localized invalid-IV effects, under an anchor constraint that keeps at least one relevant instrument valid on every simplex. A distributed algorithm parallelizes the computation over simplices for two- and three-dimensional images. We study the asymptotic properties of Hi-FIVE, establish consistency and pointwise asymptotic normality, and construct bootstrap-calibrated simultaneous confidence regions whose finite-sample coverage is evaluated through simulations. Hi-FIVE is illustrated with an analysis of the effect of phosphorylated tau on FDG-PET imaging in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, interpreted under the stated IV assumptions.

title: Economics of Selection in Ranking & Selection: Neither Fixed-Precision nor Fixed-Budget
summary: Ranking and selection (R&S) has evolved tremendously over the last several decades, with applications in agriculture, discrete optimization with computer simulation, clinical trial design, and other areas. We challenge a widely accepted classification of R&S procedures into two categories: fixed-precision and fixed-budget. We discuss a third class, economics-of-selection (EoS) procedures, which is conceptually distinct and is found in the extant literature on Bayesian hypothesis testing and simulation optimization. Procedures in this third class seek to optimally balance two quantities: the cost of learning about the performance of each alternative and the quality of the alternative ultimately selected on the basis of that learning. Fixed-precision and fixed-budget procedures tend to optimize one of these quantities while constraining the other. We clarify these differences and show why they matter. We then present new frequentist R&S procedures in this third category, including both two-stage procedures and a sequential heuristic, assuming Gaussian observations with either known or unknown variances. We find that EoS is not a question of Bayesian versus frequentist analysis, asymptotic versus finite-sample analysis, finite-stage versus fully sequential procedures, or comparing one mean with a standard versus comparing multiple alternatives. We identify opportunities for further R&S research.

title: Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects
summary: We study the regression of a scalar response $Y$ on a Euclidean predictor $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a random predictor object $\mathcal{Z}$ in a general metric space under arbitrary structural dependence. We introduce a joint sufficient dimension reduction $(\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{X}, \mathcal{G}_Z)$ constructed via a sequential conditional independence framework, which differs fundamentally from the ordinary central subspace of $Y \mid \mathbf{X}$. Methodologically, $\mathcal{Z}$ is embedded into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and a regularized kernel-response envelope model extracts a finite-dimensional reduction of the feature map. Partial adaptive estimation then recovers the Euclidean reduction conditional on the first-stage coordinates. We establish root-$n$ consistency rates for the first-stage envelope subspace under a shrinking regularizer, alongside large-sample consistency for the second-stage Euclidean subspace estimator. Simulations and two real-data applications illustrate the utility and flexibility of the proposed method.

title: Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
comments: 23 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24057230
summary: Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $α\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Grünwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $α=1$. Our main theoretical result shows that for $α<1$ the influence of the unknown initial infectious count vanishes, but no faster than $t^{-α}$; after 332 daily steps it is about $4.4\times10^{8}$ times larger at $α=0.9$ than at $α=1$. In out-of-sample forecasting over 27 weekly origins, the effect of memory depends on the setting. In Bangladesh the integer order gives the lowest error for linear and constant-rate forecasts in 47 of 48 settings. In the United States, where reported cases reached about 18% of the population, a fractional order lowers the linear forecaster's error in all 12 comparisons in 2021 but raises the constant-rate forecaster's, with no difference significant after Holm adjustment. Against standard baselines, the SIR-based linear forecaster was more accurate than the classical SIR model and a neural network without SIR structure, and competitive with ARIMA: in the United States the fractional linear forecaster had the lowest error of all methods (seven-day MAPE 7.54% against 9.14% for ARIMA), whereas in Bangladesh ARIMA had the lowest MAPE, with no significant difference from ARIMA in either country. The choice of a fractional order should rest on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit.

title: Testing isotropy of random fields with values in abstract spaces
summary: We study the problem of testing isotropy, i.e., distributional invariance under orthogonal transformations, for random fields taking values in abstract spaces. We propose a novel approach based on computing local directional characteristics, which are uniformly distributed under the assumption of isotropy. Our work is motivated by an application in material science, where we are testing the isotropy of function-valued porosity profiles of paper sheets, whose morphology is resolved by $μ$-CT imaging. While considerably more general, the presented methodology is competitive with existing isotropy tests for real-valued random fields.

title: A Bayesian approach for checking and estimating block designs in agricultural experiments
summary: Spatial blocking is a common technique used in designed agricultural experiments. Spatial blocking, however, requires important assumptions about the spatial dependence patterns in the field. Statistical models of blocked agricultural experiments often show spatial structure in the residuals, suggesting that the original model may benefit from additional assumptions regarding the spatial dependence patterns present in the field. We propose a Bayesian model for checking block membership and estimating spatial patterns missing in the original block design. Our model is particularly motivated by cases with mis-specified blocks. To accomplish this, we embed a regression tree within a Bayesian statistical model to estimate spatial effects with a block-like spatial structure. We illustrate the benefits of our model using simulated data mimicking four typical scenarios we have encountered in our applied experience in agricultural research and using two datasets generated from designed agricultural experiments. We found that our model may serve two purposes: validating the originally designed block layout, or mis-specified block-like spatial structures. Thus, our model provides researchers with a novel tool for analyzing data from designed agricultural experiments.

title: Cotangent-lift inference of stochastic microbial dynamics
summary: We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimator of the Euler scheme, with the observations taken as the states, coincides with the regression of log-increments on abundances used in the literature, and we characterise what this estimator cannot see under measurement noise: for the linearised dynamics, the law of consecutive pairs of observations is invariant along an explicit one-parameter family of relaxation rates and noise levels, and the regression converges to a limit set by the noise. Treating the true abundances as latent, we compute the likelihood with a Gaussian moment filter and show that measurement noise is precisely what couples the filter states across samples. The exact gradient is then the backward recursion of the discrete cotangent lift, whose cost, two to three likelihood evaluations, does not depend on the number of parameters, and we give the covector map of each filter step in closed form. In simulations, the latent estimator recovers the relaxation times, noise levels and interaction strengths that the regression biases, while larger communities require prior information on the interactions. In gut microbiome time series it attributes most of the variability of a dominant genus to measurement noise and estimates its relaxation time at about $64$ hours, with a large standard error.

title: Measuring Kaplan--Meier Overestimation Under Competing Risks: Event Ordering, Quantification, and Exact Inference
summary:
Competing risks arise when individuals may experience multiple mutually exclusive event types. Competing events are frequently treated as censoring and analysed using Kaplan--Meier (KM) methods, which overestimate real-world event risks. While the existence of KM overestimation is well known, its determinants, magnitude, and inferential properties remain poorly characterised.
  We develop a nonparametric framework that treats competing risks overestimation as a statistical quantity in its own right. We show that competing event frequency alone is insufficient to characterise KM overestimation and develop an event ordering theory describing how temporal event allocation influences overestimation. Based on these results, we derive a closed-form Total Overestimation Diagnostic (TOD) that quantifies total KM overestimation directly from routine survival analysis output. We establish exact error equivalence results for both cause-specific and total overestimation. In particular, Product Limit Error Equivalence shows that inference for TOD reduces exactly to ordinary overall survival estimation.
  Simulation experiments validate the theoretical results and show that independent censoring primarily affects precision rather than overestimation magnitude. Across six benchmark competing risks datasets, cause-specific overestimation is characterised by both total overestimation and temporal event allocation. These results provide a practical framework for assessing competing risks relevance and determining when cumulative incidence methods should be preferred to naïve KM risks.
  The proposed framework transforms competing risks overestimation from a qualitative warning into a measurable quantity that can be routinely quantified, interpreted, and incorporated into reporting practice.

title: Bayesian Multinomial Logistic Normal Additive Regression for Microbiome Data Analysis
summary:
Longitudinal microbiome studies often seek to separate background temporal variation from nonlinear perturbation-associated dynamics while accounting for the count-compositional nature of sequencing data. We introduce \textit{MultiAddGPs}, a semi-parametric Bayesian multinomial logistic-normal framework that combines linear effects with additive Gaussian process components. We first prove that MultiAddGPs remain within the Marginally Latent Matrix-T Process class (MLTP) and derive the collapsed and uncollapsed representations needed for scalable inference with the Collapse--Uncollapse (CU) sampler. We then develop a back-sampling procedure for efficient posterior inference on the individual additive components. We further develop approximate maximum marginal likelihood and penalized maximum marginal likelihood procedures for hyperparameter estimation in this broader class of models. In simulations, MultiAddGPs provides accurate posterior inference and calibrated uncertainty while scaling more effectively than existing GP-based additive alternatives. Applications to two longitudinal microbiome studies demonstrate how the model separates background temporal variation from intervention-associated dynamics, including travel-associated perturbations in a human gut time series and starvation effects
  in an artificial gut system. Our methods are implemented in the \textit{fido} package on CRAN.

title: Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Exit Games with Singular Belief Dynamics
summary: We study a two-player nonzero-sum stochastic exit game with asymmetric information. Each firm chooses the time to exit a duopoly and, conditional on remaining active, when to exit a monopoly. The asymmetry stems from privately observed exit values, while profit flows are driven by a general one-dimensional diffusion. Allowing for exit from monopoly induces singular dynamics of the associated belief process, so we construct it as a limit of regular approximations. The underlying dynamics are not described by a system of SDEs, which requires a new mathematical approach. We construct a symmetric Nash equilibrium in which the duopoly exit is a hitting time of the belief process while the monopoly exit is described through the underlying diffusion. Our equilibrium exhibits novel phenomena: the market may be abandoned by both firms in finite time (market collapse), and firms with heterogeneous exit values may optimally exit simultaneously (clustering). These features are absent when monopoly is always preferred to exit.

title: Asian option valuation under price impact
summary: We develop a model for arithmetic and geometric Asian option valuation with external order flow and dealer execution costs. We first formulate it as a discrete model and then obtain its continuous time scaling limit. We derive an explicit geometric Asian option formula under a consistent price system and formulate the dealer's bid and ask through utility indifference with constrained stock trading. We identify sufficient conditions for finite reservation prices and prove absence of arbitrage under the dealer's stock trading rules. Increasing initial inventory lowers both the reservation bid and the ask in the cases studied. In the finite-step calculations, higher temporary costs and greater risk aversion widen the spread for both payoffs, with a smaller change in the midpoint of the quotes.
